note: A driver is a project fact that changes the spec. Explanations are plain sentences; chapter numbers point to the knowledge base.

drivers.label: New construction
drivers.explain: New building work. Most sections apply; see chapter 201 for section scope.

drivers.label: Addition
drivers.explain: New work joined to an existing building; new envelope and transitions to existing.

drivers.label: Alteration
drivers.explain: Changes inside or to an existing building; existing conditions and demolition apply (chapter 406).

drivers.label: Repair
drivers.explain: Fixing existing work to a defined condition; often unit prices and opening up (chapter 406).

drivers.label: Restoration
drivers.explain: Returning existing work to an earlier state; method and materials matter more (chapter 406).

drivers.label: Historic resource
drivers.explain: Treatment is judged against preservation standards and may need a review process (chapter 406).

drivers.label: Occupied during work
drivers.explain: People stay in the building; phasing, protection, noise and access apply (chapter 205).

drivers.label: Group A (assembly)
drivers.explain: Places of assembly; egress and finishes are tighter.

drivers.label: Group B (business)
drivers.explain: Offices and similar; general requirements apply.

drivers.label: Group E (educational)
drivers.explain: Schools and daycare; finishes, hardware and signage are tighter.

drivers.label: Group I (institutional)
drivers.explain: Care and detention; hardware, fire ratings and infection control apply.

drivers.label: Group M (mercantile)
drivers.explain: Stores; egress and display conditions apply.

drivers.label: Group R-1 (transient)
drivers.explain: Hotels and similar; fire separation and sound apply.

drivers.label: Group R-2 (apartments)
drivers.explain: Apartments and similar; fire separation, sound and accessibility apply.

drivers.label: Group S (storage)
drivers.explain: Storage; fire separation and sprinkler rules are the main drivers.

drivers.label: Type IA
drivers.explain: Noncombustible, highest ratings. Wood only where allowed by the code (chapter 401).

drivers.label: Type IB
drivers.explain: Noncombustible, lower ratings than IA. Rated steel usually needs protection (chapter 401).

drivers.label: Type IIA
drivers.explain: Noncombustible, unrated structure. Wood limited to allowed uses such as blocking.

drivers.label: Type IIB
drivers.explain: Noncombustible, no required ratings. Wood limited to allowed uses such as blocking.

drivers.label: Type IIIA
drivers.explain: Combustible framing allowed; exterior walls noncombustible.

drivers.label: Type IIIB
drivers.explain: Combustible framing and exterior walls allowed.

drivers.label: Type IV (heavy timber)
drivers.explain: Heavy timber structure with noncombustible exterior walls.

drivers.label: Type VA
drivers.explain: Combustible structure with ratings.

drivers.label: Type VB
drivers.explain: Combustible structure without required ratings.

drivers.label: Sprinklered
drivers.explain: Automatic sprinklers; affects some ratings and finishes (chapter 401).

drivers.label: Masonry repair
drivers.explain: Repointing, unit replacement, cleaning or sealing masonry walls (chapter 406).

drivers.label: Roofing repair or replacement
drivers.explain: Roof covering, flashing or accessories being replaced or repaired.

drivers.label: Window repair or replacement
drivers.explain: Windows, frames or their seals are being repaired or replaced.

drivers.label: Concrete repair
drivers.explain: Spalls, cracks or balcony and slab edge repair.

drivers.label: Waterproofing repair
drivers.explain: Below-grade, plaza or balcony waterproofing being repaired.

drivers.label: Sealant replacement
drivers.explain: Joint sealants being removed and replaced.

drivers.label: Coatings repair
drivers.explain: Paint or other coating preparation and recoating.

drivers.label: Door repair or replacement
drivers.explain: Doors, frames or hardware being repaired or replaced.

drivers.label: Interior repair
drivers.explain: Interior finishes or partitions being repaired.

drivers.label: AIA contract family
drivers.explain: Assumes AIA general and owner–contractor forms (chapter 301).

drivers.label: Other contract family
drivers.explain: Not AIA. The survey does not yet offer variants for it.

drivers.label: A101 + A201
drivers.explain: Stipulated-sum owner–contractor agreement with the General Conditions (chapter 301). Verify variant with Jimmy.

drivers.label: A102 + A201
drivers.explain: Cost-of-the-work with a maximum price; the owner shares more of the risk. Verify variant.

drivers.label: A104 (abbreviated)
drivers.explain: Short form for small projects. Verify variant.

drivers.label: A105 (small project)
drivers.explain: For small projects with a simpler General Conditions. Verify variant.

drivers.label: A141 (design-build)
drivers.explain: Owner and design-builder agreement. Verify variant.

drivers.label: CM (A133/A134)
drivers.explain: Construction manager forms; work is often bid in packages. Verify variant.

drivers.label: Design-bid-build
drivers.explain: Full book bid to a contractor; competition rules apply to named products (chapter 301).

drivers.label: CM at risk
drivers.explain: Bid packages and early works; the CM's role appears in Division 01.

drivers.label: Design-build
drivers.explain: Performance criteria lead; the design-builder writes much of the construction spec.

drivers.label: Demo: long-life
drivers.explain: Demo driver set by a demo option.

drivers.label: Demo: fully adhered
drivers.explain: Demo driver set by a demo option.

drivers.label: Demo: adhered attachment
drivers.explain: Demo driver set by a demo option.

drivers.label: Demo: mechanical attachment
drivers.explain: Demo driver set by a demo option.
